entry.title: Deploying a Hexo + Midnight Blog: Build from Source or Publish Static Files?
entry.summary: A maintainable Hexo + Midnight blog depends on separating source, the public build, hosting, and DNS. Compare Vercel source builds with a separate static-artifact repository, then verify the release boundary.

entry.title: CODEOWNERS rules do not accumulate: the last matching line changes the reviewers
entry.summary: GitHub CODEOWNERS assigns reviewers by path pattern, with the last matching rule taking precedence. Put multiple optional owners for one pattern on the same line, and remember that a pull request uses the target branch's version.

entry.title: Why is an S3 multipart ETag not the MD5 of the whole file?
entry.summary: An S3 multipart ETag identifies a completed object but is not guaranteed to be the whole-file MD5. Choose a checksum algorithm and full/composite type when initiating the upload, then validate the stored checksum on completion and retrieval.

entry.title: A GitHub Environment can delay deployment secrets, but only when the job references it
entry.summary: A GitHub Actions job that references an environment must pass its protection rules before it can run or access that environment's secrets. Repository visibility and plan affect which rules are available.

entry.title: Why has AbortSignal.timeout not expired after a page was suspended?
entry.summary: AbortSignal.timeout measures active time, not simply wall-clock time. Its clock pauses while a document is in the back-forward cache or a Worker is suspended, so it is not an absolute server-side deadline.

entry.title: SQS heartbeats can reduce premature redelivery, but the 12-hour limit does not reset
entry.summary: An SQS visibility timeout is a lease-like way to hide a message temporarily, not a processing lock. Renewals remain subject to a 12-hour ceiling from the first ReceiveMessage, so consumers must plan for duplicate delivery and delayed retries.

entry.title: SQS FIFO's five-minute deduplication protects send retries, not business side effects
entry.summary: Amazon SQS FIFO uses a message deduplication ID to prevent duplicate enqueueing within a five-minute window. It does not make a consumer's charge or database write happen once, and content hashing excludes message attributes.

entry.title: Python audit hooks can log and abort events, but they cannot sandbox the interpreter
entry.summary: Python 3.12's sys.addaudithook is intended for runtime auditing. An existing hook can prevent a new hook from being installed without an explicit error, so the security boundary still belongs outside the interpreter.

entry.title: Node.js permissions can limit a process, but they are not a sandbox for hostile code
entry.summary: Node.js 22's --permission can reduce accidental access to files, child processes, and Workers in trusted programs. The official documentation explicitly says it is not a security boundary against malicious code.

entry.title: The CMake generator expression is valid, so why did it not expand?
entry.summary: Generator expressions are evaluated during generation and only in supported properties or command contexts. Command-argument parsing happens first, so quoting may matter.

entry.title: Why does CI still download dependencies after adding a Docker cache mount?
entry.summary: A BuildKit cache mount is reclaimable builder-local performance state, not an image layer or an exported --cache-to cache. A fresh CI builder may start empty.

entry.title: Why does an EventBridge target stop retrying after five minutes by default?
entry.summary: EventBridge stops delivery when either the retry-attempt or event-age limit is reached. A DLQ must be configured explicitly, and a successful retry does not guarantee exactly-once side effects.

entry.title: A CRD apply succeeds but a field disappears: check schema pruning first
entry.summary: A structural OpenAPI schema defines what a CRD persists. Unknown fields may be pruned before storage unless a specific subtree explicitly preserves them.

entry.title: Why does kubectl debug need separate permission to add a container to a running Pod?
entry.summary: Kubernetes adds an ephemeral container through the pods/ephemeralcontainers subresource. Permission to patch a Pod does not automatically grant this diagnostic capability.

entry.title: A Server-Side Apply conflict says a field has an owner, not that it can never change
entry.summary: SSA records field managers. A conflicting value is rejected, while force transfers ownership; first clarify controller responsibilities before using force-conflicts.

entry.title: The test clock moved forward, so why is the Promise still pending?
entry.summary: Node's test-runner MockTimers controls selected timer and Date APIs, but setTime, tick, and Promise microtasks are distinct. Decide which wait your test must drive.

entry.title: A metric chart shows a spike but no request: what does an OpenTelemetry exemplar connect?
entry.summary: An exemplar attaches a selected measurement to a metric point and can carry trace and span IDs. It helps jump from an aggregate to a trace without storing a span for every request.

entry.title: Redis WAIT returned 2; why is the write still not necessarily durable?
entry.summary: WAIT checks replica acknowledgments for earlier writes on the current connection. The caller must check the returned count; this improves safety but does not guarantee strong consistency or persistence.

entry.title: Why is the old file still there after DELETE succeeded in a versioned S3 bucket?
entry.summary: In a versioned S3 bucket, DELETE without versionId usually creates a delete marker. Recovery removes that exact marker; permanently deleting old versions is a separate operation.

entry.title: Why does changing a Terraform for_each key plan to replace a cloud resource?
entry.summary: A for_each key becomes part of a Terraform resource address. Renaming it can look like one instance was removed and another added; use a moved block or state mv for a deliberate rename.

entry.title: TypeScript `satisfies` checks a config without widening it to a broad interface
entry.summary: `satisfies` checks compatibility while preserving the expression's inferred result. It catches missing keys and bad value types, but is neither runtime validation nor an escape from inference rules.

entry.title: Why can a long loop still block inside requestIdleCallback?
entry.summary: Use a four-item queue to explain cooperative idle budgets, separating an unexecuted page from an executed timeout-policy fixture.

entry.title: How can a selected CTest test bring its setup and cleanup along?
entry.summary: Verify fixture setup and cleanup added for selected consumers, including failed preparation and independent logs.

entry.title: Why do files written to a writable RUN bind mount vanish in the next step?
entry.summary: Verify RUN bind-write lifetime with separate output paths, a read-only failure, and a stage-source control.

entry.title: How can check-ignore explain a rule match for an already-tracked file?
entry.summary: Diagnose ignore patterns separately from index state, including verbose negated-pattern output.

entry.title: Why does Base64 Strict still accept a newline?
entry.summary: Check valid bits, invalid bits, CRLF and unpadded forms against the precise Strict contract in an unexecuted Go fixture.

entry.title: Why does O_CREATE leave the old suffix after a shorter write?
entry.summary: Distinguish creation, overwriting, truncation and append with independent full-content oracles in an unexecuted Go fixture.

entry.title: Why does Read start at ab after ReadAt returned cd?
entry.summary: Separate offset reads, sequential progress and explicit Seek with interleaved byte and short-read oracles; Go fixture unexecuted.

entry.title: Why can inputs remain outside a form after their fieldset gets a form attribute?
entry.summary: Inspect the owners of an external fieldset and its inputs, then test an unmatched explicit form override inside a form.

entry.title: HTTP 414: why can a long query still fail after the body is emptied?
entry.summary: Compare three local ASCII-target cases, distinguish URI length from content capacity, and identify evidence needed for repeated 414 responses.

entry.title: Why does a JSON reviver visit children before their parent?
entry.summary: Trace child deletion and the parent snapshot, then inspect a new array-index case without confusing deletion with compaction.

entry.title: Why can a String.raw result still contain an actual newline?
entry.summary: Compare literal segments and evaluated substitutions by exact code units, then inspect an ordinary call with fewer substitutions.

entry.title: Why can a stored string still fail isWellFormed?
entry.summary: Inspect lone and paired UTF-16 surrogates by exact units, distinguish replacement from recovery, and test a new URI-encoding consumer.

entry.title: Why does an updated image not start a rollout while a Deployment is paused?
entry.summary: Correlate paused template edits with the resumed rollout identity; the cluster fixture is unrun.

entry.title: Why can AP differ from trapezoidal area on the same PR curve?
entry.summary: Derive AP of 5/6 and trapezoidal area of 19/24 from three ranked examples, then inspect a separate tied-score condition.

entry.title: How can you restore a monkeypatch before the test ends?
entry.summary: Restore scoped patches before teardown and verify normal, exceptional, and nested-owner behavior.

entry.title: Why does ^ still use the original string origin in a fullmatch window?
entry.summary: Check original spans, sliced spans and real-newline controls to distinguish bounded matching from a new string origin.

entry.title: Why does redirect_stdout capture another thread too?
entry.summary: Separate global capture, restoration and explicit streams with a controlled joined worker and an independent stderr check.

entry.title: Why can casefold match Straße when lower cannot?
entry.summary: Separate caseless matching from original-text highlighting using expansion, offset and canonical-composition controls.

entry.title: Why is a ZINTER score eight when the inputs were one and two?
entry.summary: Use independent integer oracles and a reversed-order control to explain weighting before aggregation; Redis commands unexecuted.

entry.title: Does RestartPreventExitStatus turn a failed exit into success?
entry.summary: Separate restart prevention from successful-exit classification with two same-exit fixtures; Linux execution remains unrun.

entry.title: Why can validate_only succeed while the resource remains unchanged?
entry.summary: Compare equal success responses with different stored states and retain permission checks, request mode, and later reads.

entry.title: Why does a mute toggle keep the Mute label when aria-pressed changes?
entry.summary: Compare a stable Mute label with pressed and teaching mute states, and distinguish that design from changing action labels.

entry.title: Why can a pointer-events:none ancestor still observe its child’s click?
entry.summary: Distinguish an auto child hit from its ancestor event path, with capture and bubble logs and two physical click locations.

entry.title: How can CTest give the active phase its own timeout after waiting?
entry.summary: Verify a CTest timeout transition with fast, slow, and unmatched branches, preserving failed preflight assumptions.

entry.title: How can Docker ADD verify the expected content after a remote download?
entry.summary: Pin an approved digest, exercise matching and one-character-wrong builds, and verify exported bytes beyond download success.

entry.title: Why can Git report LF while the working file contains CRLF?
entry.summary: Read index and disk bytes independently to interpret Git EOL content fields and conversion attributes.

entry.title: Why does Marshal sort map keys despite varying iteration order?
entry.summary: Check ordinary map encoding against a fixed text oracle, including integer-to-string key conversion.

entry.title: Why does a map keep two Time keys for the same instant?
entry.summary: Compare Equal, structural equality, and normalized map keys for two location representations of one instant.

entry.title: Why can setRangeText produce the same text with different selections?
entry.summary: Compare three selection modes for one replacement and retain the text plus both endpoints before the next editing action.

entry.title: Why can a new defineProperty value resist writes and disappear from key lists?
entry.summary: Compare new descriptor and literal properties through values, flags, keys, and writes, with creation and update treated under their own conditions.

entry.title: Why do separator digits appear after splitting with a capturing regex?
entry.summary: Compare capturing and noncapturing split results, count captures against the limit, and inspect an unmatched capture.

entry.title: Why can old ReplicaSets remain with revisionHistoryLimit zero?
entry.summary: Check current Deployment completion before interpreting zero history and remaining ReplicaSets; cluster execution is unrun.

entry.title: Why can constant targets make the default R² score only zero or one?
entry.summary: Explain non-finite constant-target R² through SSE and SST, retain the replacement parameter, and compare a finite zero.

entry.title: How do you tell pytest to test an installed package by name?
entry.summary: Run pytest by package name outside its checkout and verify interpreter, installation origin, and collected tests.

entry.title: Why did the second hash include the first suffix?
entry.summary: Check copied prefix branches against complete byte inputs, an alias contamination control, and a later update after digest observation.

entry.title: Why does heapreplace evict the old minimum for an even smaller input?
entry.summary: Compare returned and retained values for two incoming scores, then verify the empty-heap startup condition.

entry.title: Why has product consumed its input before the first output?
entry.summary: Observe a finite source at construction and first-read boundaries, then distinguish zero axes from one empty axis.

entry.title: Why does unpack reject a complete frame larger than its two-byte header?
entry.summary: Compare exact and offset header decoding, a short header, payload boundaries, and incomplete fixed records.

entry.title: Why does a reverse LPOS search still return a head-based index?
entry.summary: Compare occurrence rank, head-based positions, reverse result order, and a limited MAXLEN search.

entry.title: Where can a systemd service write state with ProtectSystem=strict?
entry.summary: Keep necessary state writes in a managed directory and check an EROFS control with the same identity; Linux execution remains unrun.
